decisions.text: Hook install: tracked .githooks/ shims plus a local core.hooksPath. When node or the package is missing, the shim prints one line and exits 0, never blocking the commit, the SessionStart hook's contract. A repo with a foreign hooksPath (husky, lefthook) is reported by doctor with the reason; a backlog enhancement records that init could append the shim call into those hooks instead of stopping.

Changelog: generated only, no stored Unreleased section. A repo with no release tag yet must pass --check (an empty generated changelog is byte-stable), with a test, since every user's repo starts there. This repo's hand-written Unreleased lines are dropped.

Doc-sync dogfood: one rule, the bundle CLI and workflow (bundle.mjs, src/lib/bundle/*, bundle-phase.js, tests excluded by pathspec) require docs/playbook.md or the bundle skill staged. The rules block's doc-sync line says that a COOKWRIGHT_SKIP=doc-sync commit carries the reason in its message, since the escape itself leaves no trace.

A foreign hooks setup (core.hooksPath elsewhere or from a non-local origin, or user hooks in the hooks dir) is WARN on hooks.path with the reason, not FAIL: a chosen state, not drift; a permanent FAIL the user cannot clear trains them to ignore doctor. FAIL stays for unset (run init) and for our shim present but broken. The two file checks SKIP.

pre-push runs the single gate.checks list in this stage and prints the elapsed time on the pre-push gate line; a backlog enhancement opens for a hooks.push list that overrides gate.checks on push, since the bundle gate wants thorough and the push hook wants cheap enough never to be bypassed.

decisions.source: plan §2 disposition 7, from the plan review
decisions.text: B-002 is widened to the git hook shims rather than a new id: one bug, the package is looked for at the work tree root (node_modules/cookwright), so a workspace sub-package install or a linked worktree without node_modules prints the not-installed line.

The pre-push checks judge the working tree, never the pushed commit. Refusing a push with a dirty tree or a non-HEAD sha would breed --no-verify; each pre-push line carries '(judged on the working tree, not <sha8>)' when that is the case, the README says so, and a per-sha temporary worktree is backlogged.

Findings leave 'cookwright hook' with exit 10; the shim maps 10 to 1 and any other non-zero code to one crashed line and exit 0 (no exec), so a module-load failure never blocks a commit. A harness problem inside one check is that check's SKIP line and never changes another check's FAIL. 'secrets' runs without a config; the config-dependent checks SKIP with the loader's message.

Linked worktrees: core.hooksPath is shared repo config, so a sibling worktree whose branch lacks .githooks/ silently runs no hook (measured). Accepted as a known state doctor reports there (hooks.pre-commit FAIL missing, run init) and init repairs on that branch; no refusal and no worktree-scoped config in this stage. hooksPath scope read with --show-scope, never --show-origin (absolute path).

tools.gitleaks runs one bounded dry invocation of the staged scan at session start (output discarded, --redact kept): exit 0 or 3 is PASS, any other exit is FAIL naming the stderr line (a malformed .gitleaks.toml is drift, not a silent skip), a timeout is unverified.

Changelog release order is version order; a release's range is <previous version>..<tag>. A previous version that is not an ancestor of the next (merge-base --is-ancestor) is reported on stderr by the command and rendered anyway, deterministically.

A .githooks/pre-commit or pre-push that is neither cookwright's shim nor calls cookwright in a failure-preserving form makes the hooks setup foreign: hooks.path WARN naming it, the file checks SKIP, init writes nothing. callsCookwright accepts only exec <call>, <call> || exit 1, <call> || exit $?, or <call> as the last line; '|| true' and trailing commands are not a call.

fix:changelog applies findings 0 (the template read normalised to LF, with a CRLF-template test), 1 (unborn means HEAD is a symbolic ref whose target is absent: symbolic-ref -q HEAD succeeds and rev-parse --verify -q HEAD fails; any other git failure is a refusal through gitFailed, with a corrupt-HEAD test), 2 (version parts compared as digit strings by length then lexically, never Number), 3 (metadata read from %(contents:subject) and %(contents:body), git stripping the signature in every format; the SIGNATURE regex goes, with a parseMeta test per marker the old regex missed), 4 (the showSignature test asserts the exact argv commitsBetween passes to git, so dropping -c log.showSignature=false fails it), 5 (fs errors from changelogState and the write are Refusals, exit 2, one line '<file>: <code>', never exit 1). Finding 6 (template header vs the v1 block until s3) needs no change: s3 lands the v2 block before anything leaves the branch, and the whole-branch review checks that the template and the block agree.

Accepted as built, over the finding-3 disposition: the tag signature is cut off %(contents) by the length of %(contents:signature) (git splits it in every signing format), not read from %(contents:subject) plus %(contents:body), because the implementer measured that %(contents:subject) folds a one-paragraph tag body into one line and would merge 'released:' and 'note:' into one key. Unborn is now 'rev-parse --verify HEAD fails and symbolic-ref HEAD succeeds'; any other git state is a refusal. Plan §4.4's wording of both stays as hashed; the closeout records the two deviations. The two s1-fix strings (the '<file>: <code>' refusal detail and the README exit-code sentence) go to the developer with the s2 batch.

Accepted as built: the pathspec validation refuses ':x' and ':(prefix:N)', accepts '::x', ':(attr:…)' and an empty magic word, with the schema pattern held to the validator on 15 samples; the gate commands run with every variable of 'git rev-parse --local-env-vars' removed (15 on git 2.52), not only the plan's six; the two config SKIP notes (no cookwright.json; cookwright.json invalid: …); every changelog-check note prefixed with the file; the timed-out and unspawnable secrets notes; runGate's progress lines above the hook's gate line; gitRun env option, runGate env option, gitleaksVersion(bin), scanStaged(root, { quiet, env, cap }); FINDINGS_EXIT in shims.mjs. For s3: the README gains the 'npx cookwright hook' line in its README pass. Backlog (s3 logs it as the next B id): withDefaults replaces a non-object 'hooks' or 'gate' with the default, so the validator's 'must be an object' never fires.

For fix:hooks: when a push carries several refs, the checks run if any pushed sha is HEAD, and each line then ends with 'not tested: <refs> are not the checked-out branch' for the others; both checks SKIP only when no pushed sha is HEAD. As built, one non-HEAD ref among several makes everything SKIP, so 'git push --all' would never test; that is not what the developer's refinement intends.
The s2 strings stand as built (the hook command's lines, the shim lines, the hooks.docSync config refusals and schema descriptions), and the two fix:changelog strings with them.

Accepted as built: one shared hooksSetup reader for init and doctor with one foreignHooks message set; the three foreign init rows carrying the same reason; the hooks dir shown root-relative, dotfiles and *.sample not counted; a mode-only write that runs chmod alone; git writes carrying the inert shim paths for the refusal text, run after the file writes; the doc-sync line in header() for the implementer role (fix sessions included) with the playbook bullet; README line 5 reworded; the v1Block test helper. Open questions: the config-root versus work-tree-top placement of .githooks is logged as B-007, not folded into B-002; the loader masking a non-object hooks/gate is B-006; the several-refs pre-push behaviour stays with fix:hooks as decided.

The s3 strings stand as built: init's hooks rows and refusal, the shared foreign-hooks lines, doctor's hooks.*, tools.gitleaks, gate.scripts and homes.changelog notes, the Level 0 summary, the rules block v2 text, the implementer doc-sync line in the prompt header and the playbook, and the README sections.

fix:hooks applies: finding 0 (closes B-007: init writes the shims at the work tree top where git looks, and when the config root is below the top the shim's call is preceded by 'cd <config root, root-relative to the top>' so node_modules/cookwright and cookwright.json resolve from the config root; shimText(name, rel) and callsCookwright take the rel; doctor reads the shims at the top; hook.mjs finds the config from its cwd bounded by the top, never from the top alone; an end-to-end nested-config test commits through the real hook and checks doctor); findings 1 and 5 (every pushed sha is peeled to its commit with rev-parse <sha>^{commit}, so an annotated tag on HEAD counts as HEAD; the checks run when any peeled sha is HEAD, and each line then ends with 'not tested: <refs> are not the checked-out branch' for the others; both checks SKIP only when no peeled sha is HEAD; tests for branch plus older branch, branch plus annotated tag, tag-only push of a tag on HEAD); finding 2 (closes B-006: withDefaults applies the nested defaults only when hooks or gate is absent or an object, so a string, list or null reaches the validator and is refused; tests); finding 3 (a core.hooksPath value that is not a root-relative path inside the repo is shown as 'a path outside the repo', never verbatim); finding 6 (when git config --show-scope is refused, exit 129 or an unknown-option stderr, fall back to --local --get plus --get to tell local from elsewhere; never a Refusal, never a doctor probe error; the README names git 2.26 as the version with scopes); finding 7 (hooks.pre-commit and hooks.pre-push WARN 'the hook prints not-installed and checks nothing (npm install)' when node_modules/cookwright/bin/cookwright.mjs is absent under the directory the shim runs in); finding 8 (a vitest setup file sets GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL to a scratch file and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 for the whole suite). Finding 4 (README sections landing after the feature commits) needs no change: the plan scheduled the README in s3, and the hooks reached no user before init installed them. B-006 and B-007 move to Closed in the fix commits that close them.

CHARTER.md gains a 'Judgment rules' section as a dated amendment (2026-10-15), appended verbatim under Amendments by the orchestrator right after fix:hooks lands (s3, the session named for it, had already closed), as its own docs(charter) commit with a gate, covered by review:whole. The nine rules: (1) a harness problem never blocks the user's work, only a finding in the user's own change fails a hook; (2) drift from the declared level is FAIL, a chosen state is WARN with the reason, a FAIL the user cannot clear is a cookwright bug; (3) claim only what was measured, SKIP with the reason when the thing judged is not the thing tested; (4) logic lives in the package, the repo holds shims, config and generated files; (5) generated artifacts are never hand-maintained, derived state never stored; (6) a feature wanted twice gets built, wanted once goes to the backlog with its justification; (7) nothing private in the repo, a leak is a history rewrite; (8) escapes are per-check, named, with the reason in the commit message, --no-verify the documented last resort; (9) no runtime dependency in the core package, any dependency asked for first. From this message on the orchestrator applies these rules to every open question and review finding before escalating, cites the rule number in each recorded disposition, and escalates only what no rule covers.

Rule 3 and rule 7: accepted as built, the foreign-hooks readout uses three phrases ('an absolute path', 'a path outside the repo', "git's hooks directory") in place of the decision's one, since an absolute path inside the repo is not outside it; the withDefaults fix covers paths as well as hooks and gate. Rule 6: several config roots in one work tree (one shim fanning out to several apps) is wanted once, backlogged as E-025 with its justification. Rule 6 and rule 4: a managed shim written for another config root, or by an earlier cookwright, reads as foreign today; init refreshing a shim that carries the managed header, as it refreshes the rules block, is backlogged as E-026 and must land before shimText ever changes, since the first change would make every installed shim foreign. The unneeded COOKWRIGHT_SKIP=doc-sync on commit 323c739 (the rule did not match) is noted, harmless.

The fix:hooks strings stand as built: the foreign-hooks readout's scope and path phrases, the pre-push not-tested forms, the nested-config shim line, the doctor not-installed WARN, and the README Git hooks bullets.

Finding 0 rejected by the verifier (measured in code: git resolves a relative GIT_INDEX_FILE against the top from a subdirectory), no change. Finding 1 (rule 3, rule 6: a Windows bug nobody can measure here) is B-008. Finding 4 (rule 1 names the harm, rule 3 forbids claiming a fix unmeasured) is B-009, with the fix spelled out for a Windows runner. fix:whole applies finding 2 (rule 3 and rule 1: the staged secret scan and doctor's dry run spawn gitleaks with cwd at the work tree top, repo.top, never the nested config root, so the whole staged diff and the top-level .gitleaks.toml are what is scanned; the nested end-to-end test asserts the probe's cwd) and finding 3 (rule 3, the charter, which is later than and supersedes the ratified label of 2026-10-15 15:36: on a dirty tree both pre-push checks are SKIP 'not tested: the working tree has <N> uncommitted file(s) and is not <sha8>', nothing run; when some pushed refs are HEAD and others are not, the checks run and each line names what it tested, '<verdict> …, tested <ref> at HEAD; not tested: <others>', a PASS that names its subject rather than a footnote on another; README pre-push bullet and tests follow).
The fix:whole strings stand as built: the pre-push dirty-tree SKIP note, the 'tested … at HEAD; not tested: …' form, and the two README sentences.

decisions.source: QA round 1 follow-up, 2026-10-15, measured in a scratch repo
decisions.text: Rule 3: the device round could not exercise pre-push (the app has no remote), so the orchestrator ran the real shims end to end in a scratch repo against a local bare remote, through the bin via a node_modules/cookwright symlink: init wrote the eleven rows; the commit ran pre-commit (secrets PASS with gitleaks 8.30.1, doc-sync SKIP no rules); the first push ran the gate ('PASS gate test (0.2 s)') and 'PASS changelog CHANGELOG.md matches 0 release tag(s)'; an annotated v0.1.0 on HEAD pushed with --follow-tags gave 'FAIL changelog CHANGELOG.md: out of date with the release tags; run npx cookwright changelog and commit' and git refused the push; after 'cookwright changelog' and its commit the push passed, both lines reading 'tested main at HEAD; not tested: refs/tags/v0.1.0 is not the checked-out branch' (the tag now sits one commit behind HEAD, so that is right); a dirty tree gave 'SKIP gate not tested: the working tree has 2 uncommitted file(s) and is not <sha8>' on both checks. The generated CHANGELOG.md carried '## 0.1.0 — 2026-10-15' and the note as a blockquote. No defect.
